## Problem

`copy` voids the promise returned by `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. A rejection becomes an unhandled promise rejection, and a missing `navigator.clipboard` throws inside the click handler. Either way the button gives no feedback.

## Evidence

src/App.vue:32 `const copy = (text: string) => void navigator.clipboard.writeText(text)`. It is used by src/App.vue:84, :98 and :109. `writeText` rejects with NotAllowedError when the document is not focused or permission is denied. `navigator.clipboard` is undefined outside secure contexts (a LAN-IP `vite preview`).

## Impact

The user believes the script was copied and pastes whatever the clipboard held before into `/etc/init.d/<name>`, a file then made executable and run as root by the next step.

## Fix

Handle failure visibly. On rejection, or when `navigator.clipboard` is absent, select the matching textarea's text (`textarea.select()`) so the user can copy manually and sees what is selected. Cover both paths in the UI test with a stubbed clipboard.

## Resolution
copy() runs writeText inside a promise chain and on rejection or missing navigator.clipboard focuses and selects the textarea; both failure paths tested (selection range + activeElement); mutation M3 killed.
title: Copy buttons discard the clipboard promise; a failed copy is silent

## Problem

Most diagnostics in the generated script go to stderr, but the start-failure message, its preceding blank line, and the usage error go to stdout.

## Evidence

src/service-template.ts:73 `echo ''`, :74 `echo "Error! Could not start $NAME!"`, :136 `echo "Usage: $0 {start|stop|status|restart|uninstall}"` (followed by `exit 2`). All are stdout. Compare :53, :61 and :82, which use `>&2`.

Delete `echo ''`. Append `>&2` to the start-failure line and to the Usage line. Add a template assertion for both.

Start failure and usage now go to stderr; `echo ''` removed. Behavioural test runs `dash -s bogus` (stdout empty, stderr starts with Usage, exit 2); mutation M14 killed.

## Problem

install-script. The denial recorded for `@ivuorinen/stylelint-config` names the exact version 1.3.7. npm matches `allowScripts` keys against the resolved identity, so the installed 1.4.15 is "unreviewed", and npm 11 runs unreviewed lifecycle scripts with only a notice.

## Evidence

package.json:43 `"@ivuorinen/stylelint-config@1.3.7": false`. Lockfile: `node_modules/@ivuorinen/stylelint-config` version 1.4.15, `hasInstallScript: true`. Its manifest has `"postinstall": "node scripts/postinstall.cjs"`. `npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending` (npm 11.19.1) prints `@ivuorinen/stylelint-config@1.4.15 (postinstall: node scripts/postinstall.cjs)` as not covered. npm docs (`strict-allow-scripts`) say unreviewed entries run "with a notice". The package is first-party, under the repo owner's scope.

## Impact

The explicit denial added in c467145 lapsed silently on the first minor bump. The postinstall, which writes a starter `.stylelintrc.json` through `@ivuorinen/config-checker`, runs on every `npm ci` and `npm install`, in CI and on contributor machines.

## Fix

Replace the key with the unpinned form: `"allowScripts": { "@ivuorinen/stylelint-config": false }`. An unpinned deny survives version bumps, and the repo already commits its own `.stylelintrc.json`.

## Resolution
allowScripts key is now the unpinned "@ivuorinen/stylelint-config": false; `npm approve-scripts --allow-scripts-pending` -> "No packages with unreviewed install scripts."
title: allowScripts denial is pinned to 1.3.7; the installed 1.4.15 runs its postinstall

## Problem

mutation-blind. 'constrains the shell-bearing inputs at the boundary' passes as long as the attribute text matches. The pattern it pins is an invalid regular expression under the `v` flag that the HTML standard compiles `pattern` with, so browsers ignore it, and the test cannot notice.

## Evidence

src/__tests__/App.spec.ts:33 `expect(html.match(/pattern="\[A-Za-z0-9_\.-\]\+"/g)).toHaveLength(2)`. Node 24: `new RegExp('^(?:[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)$', 'v')` → `Invalid regular expression … Invalid character in character class`. With the `u` flag it compiles, which is why the test author's mental model held.

## Impact

The test's stated purpose ("constrains the shell-bearing inputs at the boundary") is not met in any current browser, and the suite stays green. It exists only to keep a third copy of SAFE_NAME in sync, the kind of guard around avoidable duplication the project should delete instead.

## Fix

Preferred: remove the duplicated `pattern` attributes (see the audit finding on the pattern) and replace this test with a DOM test asserting that an invalid name sets `aria-invalid="true"` and shows the field error, driven by SAFE_NAME itself. Minimal alternative: extract the attribute and assert `new RegExp(`^(?:${p})$`, 'v')` does not throw.

## Resolution
App.spec.ts and its pattern-string assertion deleted with the pattern attributes; replaced by main.spec.ts tests asserting aria-invalid and error visibility driven by SAFE_NAME; mutation M2 (invert aria-invalid) kills 4 tests.
title: Pattern test asserts the presence of a pattern that browsers reject
